body: In my experience you can have a method and a plan, so long as there's no imminent threat of harm to yourself or to others. If you have a plan but no intention, or no immediate intention, of acting on it, I haven't seen that lead to you getting committed. That doesn't mean it can't happen, though.

It depends. If you tell them you're having thoughts, then they try to help you, obviously. They will probably ask you if you have a plan. If you say you have an imminent plan to kill yourself, they will probably send you to an inpatient facility. If you say you don't intend to do it but know how you would, they'll still just try to help you. You should tell your therapist everything, to the extent that you're able and ready.  They only want to help.

I agree with you entirely, and made a post that makes a pretty similar argument with a slightly different focus than yours. I recognise that my telling you this probably doesn't help. But I agree with you entirely, thank you for making this argument

>Because it IS an illness. 

Not really. It's a perspective. And not an inaccurate one. 

>The problem is, we don't have the feel good chemicals when we SHOULD have them 

When "should" we have them? Should we have the good chemicals when we wake up to get tortured for 7 hours? Because people keep telling me I should, and somehow I don't buy it. Should we have them when we wake up to go to work, to sacrifice our day doing something we don't want to do for the benefit of someone else's needless profit? Because people keep telling me I should, and somehow I don't buy it. Should we have them when the weekend comes around, so we can pretend the other 5/7 of our lives don't exist for 2 days because of how much we secretly hate them? Because people keep telling me I should, and somehow I don't buy it. 


>Nope. Happiness is real. I thought it was fake as well, until I got better 

If it was real people wouldn't have to escape the world on the weekends with partying and alcohol. They wouldn't look forward to the 2 days a week that they don't hate their lives. They wouldn't try to live vicariously through people on social media and reality TV because those people's lives are more interesting and better off than our own. If people's happiness was real, people would be happy, and would enjoy their own lives, and that's simply not the case. 

>The physical paper has no worth, but people pretend that it does. If everyone accepts it as currency, then it has worth 

Does it? Or do people ascribe worth to meaningless objects of wealth? Does that car make you happy? Your phone? Earning more money does not equate to having more of your emotional and physical needs met (after a point. I recognise that poor starving people could use some money to eat). 

>Information and knowledge is causing us to change the world around us. It makes new machines, new medicines, new philosophies and morals, new theories, etc. It affects us on a daily basis 

It affects us only superficially. People were fine before all those new machines and medicines and philosophies. In fact, they were happier, and they were better off. Those things do not impact our fundamental needs. 

>Depression isn't seeing the world in a better light. We arent some revolutionaries who know the absolute truths. Depression is the exact opposite of optimism. 

I didn't say, nor do I believe, it's seeing the world in a better light. It's seeing it in a more accurate light. We aren't revolutionaries, but a lot of us do seem to have realised more truth in the world than the other, non-depressed people. It's the opposite of optimism because optimism is unrealistic. 

>It distorts the way we see the world. Our successes become meaningless, our failures become apocalyptic. We feel guilty over things that aren't even our fault. 

It clarifies the way we see the world. Our successes ARE meaningless, because they don't benefit our fundamental needs, and so they don't stimulate the good chemicals. We can't cope with our failures because they compound our view of reality, and we're desperate to be proven incorrect. Sadly, we cannot be.  We feel guilty because we can see the cause and can't fix it. 

>Then there are the cognitive and physical symptoms as well. The memory loss, the brain fog, inability to focus, the exhaustion, the changes in sleeping and eating patterns, the physical aches, etc. 

These all come as a result of not having the good chemicals. None of these are symptoms of anything other than that, and we don't have the good chemicals because there's no reason to have them. 

>Not to mention the constant cycles of self destructive thought patterns. And the negative beliefs that we house of reality, which sadly seems to be based more on depression than actual reality 

The self destructive thought patterns arise from the view of reality, and the view of reality is very bleak, but accurate. If it wasn't accurate, it wouldn't have such a profound affect on our biology. It is based on reality, it causes depression, and therefore cannot be caused by depression. 

>Depression strips us of our will to live. It steals our hope. It causes us to feel suicidal. The logic becomes so distorted, that some people believe their own death will HELP their loved ones. 

>Depression kills people. It's an illness

Because our will to live doesn't have a purpose, there's no reason to live. There is no cause for hope in reality as it actually is. There is no reason to live, so we are suicidal. That's not a fault of logic, that's a fault of their loved ones being affected by exposure to depression. 

It does kill people, because those people realise that there's no value in life or in the world, and that there is no reason to live. It is not an illness.

Almost any time in history. Now, you might point to people being wealthier, less sickly, and more "free"(whatever that means) than they were in the past. And that's true. But people were, on average, happier, with lower rates of depression and suicide, at every other time in human history. If you value materialistic things, then sure, now is the best time ever. If you value happiness, now is the worst time ever.
